newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Guinness sees start of turnaround.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Guinness sees start of turnaround.

text.p: British drinks group Guinness Plc is at last seeing signs of a turnaround in trading conditions for its spirits brands in mature markets, said chairman Tony Greener in an interview.
"We have seen in developed markets, and particularly in the United States, the start of a turnaround, for the first time since the early 1980's," he said.

Sales volumes at United Distillers (UD), the company's spirits arm, were up one percent in 1996 at 45.7 million cases, an increase of 0.6 million on 1995. The overall average price increase at UD in the year was around 1.5 percent and Greener made positive remarks about the climate for pricing in the coming year.
"Going forward our feeling is the climate for pricing is improving and in terms of Scotch volume we would expect to see the underlying rate of growth on Scotch sales improving again."
Greener said the company has already announced a number of price increases for the coming year, "our sense is the overall climate for price increases will be somewhat more favourable this year."
Scotch Whisky sales at 25.7 million cases were one percent below the comparable 1995 level due to deliberately reduced shipments designed to reduce trade stock levels.
"Sales of Johnnie Walker Black Label were up by six percent. So we are really seeing a good strong performance at consumer level in the States which I really think is encouraging."
The company has announced a two percent price rise in the United States, due to come into effect on July 1, for chain stores and February 1 for controlled states.
In Thailand a 1.2 percent rise has been announced and in Japan a two percent increase due on April 1, although prices in Japan were adjusted down by four percent last year.
Asia Pacific profits rose 15 percent to 184 million stg in 1996, making it the UD's largest profit region.

In Latin America prices are expected to move in line with inflation. In Spain and Portugal the company aims to get price rises of between three and four percent through on its spirits brands with effect from June 1.
In Germany, a three percent rise on Johnnie Walker is planned for the second half of the year.
"In the UK the strategy is to build the equity of our brands and lead the industry on a stronger pricing environment and we have had some good success in both of those areas last year," said Greener.
Prices on UD's spirits brands in Britain were increased seven percent last year. The company also held prices ahead of Christmas when the temptation is strongest to offer discounts, said Greener.
Profits from Britain fell nine percent to 49 million in 1996 after a big increase in marketing and the company's decision to scrap promotional offers.
Guinness spent 330 million stg on marketing at UD last year and 205 million on Guinness brewing and this double digit year-on-year increase will continue, said Greener.
"I have called it a landmark year because its a year in which a lot of the action and investment we have been taking over the last few years has started to come through," said Greener.
Earlier the company reported an 11 percent increase in its 1996 pre-tax profits to 975 million stg, in line with most brokers forecasts.
United Distillers turned in a fairly flat performance with trading profits of 678 million stg in 1996, while brewing recorded a six percent rise to 283 million.
